what_it_does: A core bottleneck in AI chips is the constant shuttling of numbers back and forth between the memory chips where data is stored and the logic circuits where math is performed — this is often called the memory-compute bottleneck. This paper proposes using light (photonics) rather than electrical signals to perform the multiply-and-add operations at the heart of neural-network math, directly inside a modified version of SRAM (the fast on-chip memory that chips already use). The design is a mixed analog-optical-digital circuit: data stored in a photonic SRAM cell modulates light to perform multiplication optically, then a novel analog-to-digital converter — called a 1-hot encoding electro-optic ADC — turns the optical result back into a digital number for further processing. Because the multiplication happens where the data lives, the expensive data-movement step is largely eliminated. The approach is exploratory and based on abstract-level claims; specific measured results are not available from the abstract alone.
